title.narrative: Support Member States in using UNESCO designated sites for bio and geo diversity

description.narrative:
Through their integrated approach to biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, sustainable development, and knowledge generation, UNESCO designated sites are at the forefront of UNESCO’s efforts to advance the Nature–Society–Development Nexus. They contribute to addressing the direct and indirect drivers of biodiversity loss and climate change, strengthening resilience to environmental and socio-economic challenges, and supporting the implementation of major global commitments, including the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the Paris Agreement, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and the United Nations Decades on Ecosystem Restoration and Ocean Science for Sustainable Development.
By bringing together interdisciplinary research, local and Indigenous knowledge systems, participatory governance, and innovative partnerships, UNESCO designated sites serve as living laboratories and learning sites for sustainable development. They generate and test solutions to contemporary environmental and development challenges, facilitate cooperation among stakeholders, promote the exchange of good practices and experiences, and contribute knowledge products, training opportunities, and capacity-development resources that support the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.
